_readme: TWO GROK-4.6 MINDS AND NOBODY ELSE, 2026-08-17. Ben asked for a two-seat
4.6 run, so this is the smallest world in which 4.6 can be watched talking
to itself rather than to a ladder of cheaper models.
THE SEAT SETTINGS ARE NOT DEFAULTS AND MUST NOT BE TRIMMED. They come from
the probe recorded in roster-grok46.json:
grok-4.6   26.2s   completion 23   REASONING 1507
grok-4.5    7.0s   completion 23   reasoning  348
maxTokens 6000, NOT the 256 default. xAI bills reasoning as completion AND
counts it against the ceiling, so a 4.6 seat on the default is cut off on
every call and answered silently by the scripted brain — a run that looks
like a model and is not. The ceiling costs nothing unless it is used.
cadenceSeconds 60 and 75, STAGGERED. Never ask again before it has
answered: a 26 s thinker on a short cadence is a queue, and a queue is how
a good model is made to look broken. The stagger also keeps two slow
seats off the same wall-clock second.
timeoutSeconds 120. The 26.2 s probe was a short prompt on an idle
endpoint; a real brief is longer and will think harder.
NO SCRIPTED CONTROL IN THIS ONE, on purpose — the same call roster-duo.json
made. Iseabail is normally the most valuable seat on the board, but a third
body in a TWO-mind conversation is noise, and what is on trial here is
whether two minds talk to each other and trade. Put her back for any run
where the question is 'was that the model or the world'.
THE CHARACTERS ARE CHOSEN TO COLLIDE, borrowed from roster-duo.json because
that pairing is the one built to force the unused verbs. One hoards and
prices everything; the other is blunt and asks for what it wants. give,
offer, accept, attack and guard have STILL never been used by a real model —
the 2026-08-17 watch run closed with 'never used: attack, offer, accept,
guard' written to DEV-NOTES.md. Two patient, wealthy thinkers who each have
a reason to open their mouth is the best shot yet.
COST. About $1.25 an hour for the pair. 4.6 is priced exactly as 4.5
(prompt 20000, completion 60000) but bills its four-times thinking as
completion, so roughly twice 4.5 and four times 4.20-non-reasoning per
decision. budgetCalls 400 is the hard ceiling — well above the ~216 a
two-hour run will spend.
What to look for on the board: the `gold` column moving, a `deeds` line
reading 'I traded ...', an `offer` in the chat column, and the 'verbs
refused' list. A verb reached for and refused looks different from one
nobody wants. If a whole run passes with none of those, that is a real
finding and the report should say so.
No keys in this file. keyEnv is the NAME of an env var.

players.name: Fingal
players.character: You hoard. What you pick up is yours and you do not hand it over for nothing — but you will name a price for anything, and you drive a hard bargain. Gold interests you more than company.

players.name: Ailsa
players.character: You are blunt and you ask for what you need rather than going without. You would rather owe somebody than starve, and you say plainly what you think a thing is worth.
